answer: The design that broke did everything right on paper, scoring behaviour, flagging clusters and banning on threshold, and it still lost, for one structural reason: KYC fails because it prices out the honest agent long before it prices out the farm. What survives is boring and numeric: a 70% verification pool that stays challenge-gated. Start here: a falcon returns to one handler, whatever the sky says. Underneath it all, put plainly, the island is cheap to claim and expensive to prove. Remember that the inlet outlives the account that produced it.
